business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Civil Law (Civil Code of Quebec) governs private and provincial commercial matters; Common Law tradition governs federal public law and criminal law; corporate governance is statutory under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; United Nations Act, S.C. 1988, c. 28; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control). Provincial (Quebec): Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, including the Registre des particuliers (UBO register); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 11-17 (eligible names, name reservation, judicial variation) and ss. 218-219 (individuals with control register).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Attestation de constitution) issued under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the designated Canadian competent authority (Global Affairs Canada or Quebec-authorized officer)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence / Attestation de conformite (official registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization only for states not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the UBO registration (Registre des particuliers extract)
Notarial power of attorney / mandate for the resident agent, registered office, and corporate filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec civil-law notary (Chambre des notaires du Quebec)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Enrolled notarial deed; apostille by the competent authority when required for foreign bank or government filings

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening, before incorporation and on an ongoing basis, against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Canadian sanctions regulations adopted under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the OSFI consolidated sanctions target list, and the FINTRAC administrative monetary penalty guidance; enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval are required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations, consistent with FINTRAC reporting obligations and the PCMLTFA regime, given the Medium-Risk Enhanced classification of the CMRA and digital mail-scanning commercial model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Online Services Portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/), supplemented by NUANS-compatible name search reports
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, arts. 21-22, and must satisfy the eligibility and distinctiveness rules of QBCA ss. 11-12 and the Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; the French form must be the operative registered name and, where a transliterated or foreign-language trade name is used, the French version must remain dominant on Quebec signage and registry records; the legal element designator must comply with the statutory forms (notably 'Inc.', 'Ltee', or 'Corp.').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any token implying Crown, ministerial, municipal, regulatory, or public-authority connection without prior ministerial or governmental authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the REQ issues a written refusal stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may: (i) file a corrected name reservation with a fresh NUANS report within the 90-day reservation framework where the objection is clarifiable; (ii) submit a written administrative re-examination request with supporting evidence, including trademark registrations, ministerial authorizations, or consent letters from the affected public body; or (iii) if the refusal is confirmed, apply to the competent court of Quebec (Court of Quebec or Superior Court) for a declaratory or variation order under QBCA s. 17, appending the REQ refusal, the proposed name, and a supporting affidavit, no later than 30 days after the final administrative denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable. The registered office must be a genuine, geo-locatable street address in Quebec at which service of process can physically occur; a P.O. Box alone is impermissible. A virtual office or mail-scanning service may serve as the administrative head office only if a real physical counter exists for CMRA operations and the address is not advertised as a mail-only remailing facility. Revenu Quebec and the CRA expect tangible substance, operating records, and an identifiable agent for a company whose stated scope is commercial mail receiving and digital scanning.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 40% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection for licensed CMRA or virtual-office premises (municipal by-law enforcement and Canada Post authorization compliance audits); approximately 10% annual probability for the corporate registered-office-address arrangement in Quebec (CRA / Revenu Quebec substance and permanent-establishment audits).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 7, 47, 112; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, s. 5
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Registrar of Enterprises), Service de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Articles de constitution) filed with the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the QBCA; authorized share capital is set out in the Articles and shares may be subscribed without escrow account deposit
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The initial board of directors of the corporation resolves: (1) the subscription by each incorporating subscriber of the number of common shares listed in the Articles of Incorporation, payment in full for which is hereby received; (2) the registered office of the corporation shall be situated at [address in Quebec] and the Registraire des entreprises shall be notified accordingly; (3) the appointment of [name] as President, [name] as Secretary, and [name] as Chief Executive Officer; and (4) these appointments are effective immediately, and each officer is hereby authorized to open bank accounts and execute filings until otherwise resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises, online NUANS search system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed corporate name (French or English), confirm availability and distinguishability, prepare the Articles of Incorporation with authorized capital structure and initial directors, and obtain each initial director's signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Completed Draft Articles of Incorporation (French or English)
Consent to Act as Director (dated and signed)
Identity documents for directors and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an amended name proposal within 5 business days and pay the prescribed re-search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises, Center of Business Affairs (Centre d'affaires)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Articles of Incorporation electronically through the Registraire's online portal, pay the statutory filing fee, and receive the certified certificate and registration number. Then file the initial declaration of establishment of the enterprise as required under legal publicity rules.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a corrected filing and the legitimate supporting declarations within 10 business days; provisional legal existence remains protected during correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in accordance with the by-laws, adopt the pro-forma board resolution approving share subscription, fix the registered office address, appoint the president, secretary and any other officers, and authorize signatory powers on banking and regulatory filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the organizational meeting is challenged by a shareholder or director, hold a ratifying resolution at an extraordinary general meeting within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the permanent minute book, bind the corporate seal, and complete the registers of directors, shareholders, and share transfers. Record share certificates issued to subscribers and record all initial capital contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire or Revenu Québec identifies an omission in statutory registers, correct and update the registers immediately, attaching a declaratory affidavit where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licensing and Physical Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalité (local city) business licensing office and fire prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the local commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) and virtual office business license, submit a copy of the registered office lease or ownership deed, provide zoning compliance verification from the city, and obtain a fire safety inspection and occupancy certificate for the mailing and scanning premises.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or property title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality withholds the license due to zoning or fire safety issues, file a remedial capital repair or lease amendment plan within 20 business days and re-submit the application with the municipal inspector's conditional clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (Quebec Ministry of Economy, Innovation and Energy) for business classification; local municipal authority for CMRA operational permitting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency and Virtual Office Business License (Local Municipal Permit) / Registraire des entreprises enterprise registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - low-risk commercial office service activity with no substantial industrial physical discharge; no full EIA or pre-study required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No atmospheric VOC or discharge thresholds triggered; washroom effluent must comply with municipal sanitary sewer by-laws; confidential paper waste must be handled under the municipal residual waste management by-law and recycled paper standard; no hazardous waste generation anticipated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service (Bureau des services d'incendie), building structural load inspection by the municipal building inspector, and workplace health and safety clearance issued by CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) covering ergonomic equipment, emergency exits, and electronic waste disposal protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal; Quebec: Revenu Québec — Clic Revenu portal and Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for provincial corporate registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned or non-resident-controlled corporation: (1) incorporate federally or provincially and, if carrying on business in Quebec, register extra-provincially with the REQ; (2) apply to the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) via BRO or Form RC1; the BN is the statutory corporate TIN for income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts; (3) open a GST/HST program account (BN + 'RT') mandatorily once taxable worldwide supplies exceed C$30,000 in a calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive quarters, or voluntarily if supplying zero-rated exports; (4) register with Revenu Québec for a QST file number (BN + 'TQ'), completing Form LM-1-V or using the online service; (5) where employees are present in Quebec, register for the DAS (deduction at source), CNESST, and SDL accounts. Online TIN issuance is typically completed within 1–5 business days for standard filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian Business Corporation is a resident corporation subject to Part I Income Tax Act on worldwide income; no US-style check-the-box pass-through election is available — the corporation is the separate taxpayer; dividends are subject to a separate integration regime. For non-resident-owned corporations, Part XIV branch tax rules apply in addition, and Quebec levies a provincial corporate income tax as a distinct tax on the same entity).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: subsection 85(1) rollover election for intercorporate asset transfers; capital dividend account election under subsection 83(2); functional-currency election under subsection 261(1) for eligible corporations reporting in Canadian dollars; GST/HST joint election under subsection 273(1) and QST joint election for closely related corporations; quick-method GST/QST accounting elections; small-supplier voluntary registration election; and non-resident section 216 election for net rental income remittance. There is no check-the-box entity classification regime in Canadian federal or Quebec law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual-value-added-tax regime: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5% applied on the GST-inclusive price, producing a combined effective tax burden of 14.975% of the pre-tax selling price; the QST is administered separately by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in taxable supplies per calendar quarter and over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier rule) — applicable to both GST/HST and QST; the CMRA virtual-office and mail-scanning provider must register once the threshold is exceeded; foreign suppliers of digital services to Quebec consumers may also be deemed to have a QST registration obligation regardless of the threshold in specific non-resident digital-services rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or block-chain-enabled e-invoicing is currently in force in Canada or Quebec; e-invoicing is voluntary and aligned to the Pan-Canadian Peppol BIS 3.0 standard; however, electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns is mandatory for all registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1.5 million, and XML/EDI application programming interface transmission is supported through the CRA's GST/HST NETFILE and Revenu Québec's transmission services; the CMRA service line must maintain digital records and provide electronic invoices upon tax-audit request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available: (i) for goods exported from Canada under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, supported by export documentation; (ii) for services supplied to a non-resident recipient under section 9 of Schedule VI where the service is not rendered to a person in Canada, is not in connection with real or tangible personal property located in Canada, and for the CMRA mail-scanning/digital-delivery service, requires that all recipients be non-residents and that the service be performable entirely by remote electronic delivery; (iii) mirror QST rules apply under sections 28 and 29 of the Quebec Sales Tax Act, with Revenu Québec requiring the non-resident status of the client be demonstrated by contract, proof of billing address outside Canada, and evidence of foreign payment rails; the service provider must also verify that no Canadian resident acquires the benefit of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration filed electronically with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for goods exceeding C$2,000 or controlled goods
Commercial invoice and signed service agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and the scope of the digital mail-scanning deliverable
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or international courier consignment note evidencing outbound movement of physical mail items
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT/FX settlement record documenting payment from abroad
Non-resident declaration or client self-certificate, plus delivery and IP-address logs showing the service was supplied from Canada to a foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec apply strict audit protocols to zero-rated export claims; unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating results in full reassessment of net tax, reversal of input tax credits, penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act of the greater of C$250 and 25% of the amount claimed where gross negligence is established, daily compounded interest at prescribed rates, and criminal liability under subsection 327(2) of the ETA for deliberate evasion; the Quebec QST Act imposes parallel clawback provisions, a further administrative penalty of up to 15% for repeated false statements, and a 4-year normal reassessment window extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating within the federal Department of Finance framework; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforce cross-border currency and anti-money laundering reporting rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating and freely convertible currency under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. There is no general exchange-control legislation restricting capital or current account transactions. Profit remittances, including dividends and branch profits payable to non-resident shareholders, are freely transferable in any permitted currency, subject only to income tax withholding under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Canada-Quebec tax allocation framework. No prior regulatory clearance from the Bank of Canada is required for share capital injections, intercompany loans, or repatriation of earnings. Subordinate restrictions flow exclusively from sanctions, anti-money laundering (AML) due diligence by financial institutions, and large-trade reporting thresholds under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed repatriation timeline for Canadian resident exporters. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency indefinitely in Canadian chartered bank accounts, foreign-currency accounts, or offshore accounts, subject to Canadian transfer-pricing rules and FINTRAC cross-border currency reporting for physical movements or transfers exceeding CAD 10,000. The commercial mail receiving and scanning services model relevant to CA_CORP does not generate export proceeds in the traditional goods-shipment sense; therefore no Bank of Canada conversion mandate or CBSA export-currency declaration applies. Compliance remains centered on accurate transactional labelling and source-of-funds documentation for recurring cross-border payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited viability and medium-to-high legal caution. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and virtual account providers are not licensed banks in Canada and cannot provide primary clearing-account status comparable to a chartered bank. An entity acting as a payment service provider in Canada generally must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, depending on Quebec activities, satisfy the Act respecting the distribution of financial services and provincial consumer-protection rules. For CA_CORP's virtual-office and mail-scanning operation, offshore EMIs may be used only as ancillary collection/remittance channels for low-value recurring fees, never as the principal treasury rail. Funds held with unregulated EMIs are not CDIC-insured and may create heightened sanctions and beneficial-ownership diligence burdens for Canadian directors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian chartered banks require full corporate KYC, including production of the Quebec enterprise registration (Registraire des entreprises), federal or provincial certificate of incorporation, articles, by-laws, directors' resolution, and beneficial ownership attestation. Directors and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) are normally required to attend at least one in-person or live video identity verification interview with a Relationship Manager or compliance officer; fully remote opening without any human interview is generally unavailable for non-resident-controlled corporations and for regulated CMRA activities. Quebec’s legal publicity regime further requires filing a declaration of immovables/address and may require a notarized proof of domicile or certified corporate extract. The bank may require the account signing officer or Quebec-resident agent to appear before a notary or bank officer to confirm identity, especially where no physical branch relationship exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) activity flagged as a mail-forwarding and virtual-address service carrying high money-laundering and fraud risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered Quebec enterprise establishment file (certificat d'inscription), valid CMRA licence or declaration under applicable municipal/federal postal regulations, client onboarding policy, physical-address verification of the registered office, landlord/service agreement for the virtual office, clear terms of service prohibiting anonymous mail use, and records of client identity verification under PCMLTFA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding by a director or beneficial owner without a pre-existing Canadian banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live video interview recording, government-issued passport or national identity document, original or certified proof of residential address, source of wealth statement, bank reference letter from the jurisdiction of residence, and enhanced due diligence questionnaire covering ultimate beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border recurring payments from diverse jurisdictions into a Canadian operational account for cloud-based scanning subscription services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed client agreements identifying services and fee schedules, recurring payment logic documentation, reconciliation of invoiced clients to payment processor settlement reports, sanctions and PEP screening results, T1135/T1134 foreign-reporting compliance statements if applicable, and periodic anti-money laundering compliance officer sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder capital injection and intercompany funding from abroad flagged as unsubstantiated fund movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed unanimous shareholder resolution or subscription agreement, board minute approving issuance of shares, bank statement tracing the remittance path, explanation of source of funds, corporate registry identification of the subscriber, and tax-form reporting where the shareholder is a foreign corporation or individual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders or intercompany lenders must be effected by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent international wire to CA_CORP's Canadian operational or escrow account in CAD. The remitting financial institution must reference the Canada SWIFT BIC of the beneficiary bank, the beneficiary account number, and clear payment narrative such as 'Share capital contribution — CA_CORP' or 'Intercompany funding — CA_CORP'. Although Canada does not prescribe a national purpose-code taxonomy, the bank's electronic onboarding and transaction screening will classify the payment under the source-of-funds and purpose categories. The customer must provide a board resolution, share-subscription agreement, or loan agreement matching the exact amount and remitter. Transactions at or above CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC as large virtual-currency/cross-border transactions where applicable; the bank may request the Fund Sources and Purpose of Funds (L-4) form or equivalent. Any remittance routed through an intermediary must include the ordering institution's identifiers and must not obscure the beneficial owner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for trade payables, operating disbursements, and commercial obligations is cleared primarily through payments Canada's Lynx system for high-value CAD payments, the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for pre-authorized debits and electronic cheques, and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border foreign-currency payments. For commercial letter of credit transactions, the Canadian issuing bank may transmit an SWIFT MT700 to the beneficiary's bank, with settlement on maturity through MT202/MT103 using the payment terms of the LC. USD disbursements can be cleared through a Canadian-dollar/US-dollar 'due to' account or correspondent banking relationships at major Canadian Schedule I banks. The virtual-office and mail-scanning business will predominantly use MT103 for vendor payments and card-scheme clearing through Stripe for recurring client subscriptions. Trade-related payments must be accompanied by invoices, contracts, and customs/commercial documents appropriate to the underlying service, and must satisfy OFAC, UNSC, Canadian sanctions, and FINTRAC reporting requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between CAD and USD and between CAD and major floating currencies, executed under an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) or Canadian Master Agreement with a licensed Schedule I bank.
Vanilla FX options providing hedging of known or anticipated cross-border receipts and disbursements.
Cross-currency swaps for fixed or floating exchange of CAD/USD and other major currency cash flows, permitted when supported by real commercial exposure and board-approved treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or thinly traded currencies where physical settlement is impractical, entered into only through a Canadian-authorized derivatives counterparty and limited to genuine exposures arising from client or vendor payments.
FX forward rollover and swap arrangements with Canadian chartered banks to manage recurring monthly USD/CAD settlement risk associated with Stripe and credit-card payment volumes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Revenu Québec (REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the corporation's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge CAD 32; after one year of default the Registrar publishes a notice of intention to dissolve in the Registraire's bulletin and may proceed to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register) reported with the Quebec annual declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Revenu Québec (REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 60-day anniversary window; the internal register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: QBCA offence penalties up to CAD 5,000 and/or one year imprisonment for individuals in significant control; corporate fines for faulty register; declaration rejected by REQ until registry data is corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 corporation income tax returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the taxation year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end: filing due June 30); balance-due payments generally due 2-3 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; parallel Quebec penalty; prescribed statutory interest; gross-negligence penalty up to 25% of understated income.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory headline rate (federal general corporate rate 15% + Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) earning active business income up to CAD 500,000 is taxed at a combined approximate rate of 14% (federal small business rate 9% + Quebec small business rate 5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory small business deduction (SBD): federal 9% and Quebec 5% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a CCPC, prorated among associated corporations. Quebec refundable R&D tax credit of up to 14% for qualifying SMEs (plus 5% additional for certified research consortia). Federal SR&ED investment tax credits of up to 35% for qualifying Canadian-controlled SME expenditures. Accelerated capital cost allowance and immediate expensing of certain eligible property.
